summary: Inventory of components identified from analyzed repositories that are valuable for UML-Codex development

components.name: Template Method Code Generator Pattern
components.value_proposition: Proven pattern for multi-language code generation. Base generator with overridable hooks scales to 10+ languages. Plugin architecture enables independent development per target language.
risks: Need Python equivalent of Xtend templates
components.notes: Core architectural pattern. Use Python/Jinja2 instead of Java/Xtend. Return Dict[filename, content] for clean separation.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Reviewed rosetta-code-generators. Pattern is excellent but technology stack needs translation to Python. Template Method pattern directly applicable.

components.name: Type Object Pattern Metamodel
components.value_proposition: Runtime metamodel with declarative type registration. Essential for UML's reflective metamodel. Enables generic model operations, validation, and serialization without hardcoding element types.
risks: May need code generation for scale
components.notes: Consider hybrid: code generation for metaclasses, Type Object pattern for runtime. Camunda manually implemented; UML scale may require generation.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Excellent reference from Camunda. Pattern works but UML scale (700+ metaclasses) suggests code generation for initial setup, then runtime reflection.

components.name: Rosetta DSL Type System
components.value_proposition: Rich type system with inheritance, composition, cardinality constraints, choice constraints. Grammar-driven with Xtext. Demonstrates how to build enterprise DSL with type safety and validation.
risks: UML already has metamodel defined by OMG spec
components.notes: Study for patterns, not direct use. UML metamodel already exists. Learn from: separation of structure/validation/logic, constraint specification, expression language design.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Excellent DSL implementation but UML doesn't need new DSL - it has OMG specification. Value is in understanding type system patterns and validation architecture.

components.name: Agenda-Based Execution Pattern
components.value_proposition: Operation queue pattern for transparent execution control. Cleaner than Camunda's PVM state machine. Operations: ContinueProcess, TakeOutgoingFlows, EndExecution. Excellent for UML Activity Diagram and State Machine execution.
components.notes: Highly applicable for UML behavioral diagram execution. Start with core operations: ExecuteAction, EvaluateGuard, ForkExecution, JoinExecution, EnterState, ExitState.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Flowable's agenda pattern superior to Camunda PVM. More debuggable, clearer execution trace. Perfect for UML Activity/State execution.

components.name: FINOS CDM Event Model Architecture
components.value_proposition: 9 primitive instructions compose complex events. TradeState with validated transitions. Applicable to UML: decompose behavioral changes into primitives, track state transitions, validate state machine semantics.
components.notes: Pattern excellent. UML primitives might be: CreateElement, DeleteElement, ModifyAttribute, AddAssociation, RemoveAssociation, ChangeState, ExecuteTransition. Build complex model changes from primitives.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Event sourcing with primitives is powerful. Enables replay, audit, validation. Directly applicable to UML model change tracking and behavioral execution.

components.name: Fluent Builder API with Recursive Generics
components.value_proposition: Type-safe method chaining: process().startEvent().serviceTask().userTask().endEvent().done(). Excellent developer experience. Reduces errors vs manual object construction.
risks: Python generics less powerful than Java
components.notes: Python equivalent using Protocol and TypeVar. Example: class ClassBuilder(Generic[T]): ... Enables: package.class_('Person').attribute('name', str).association('employer', Company).build()
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Pattern works in Python with typing.Generic and typing.Protocol. Not as clean as Java but achievable. Improves UX significantly.

components.name: Command Pattern with Interceptor Chain
components.value_proposition: All operations as commands with interceptor chain for transactions, authorization, logging, validation. Clean separation of concerns. Enables undo/redo for model editors. Perfect for UML operations.
components.notes: Simple to implement in Python. class Command(Protocol): def execute(self, context) -> T. Interceptors: TransactionInterceptor, ValidationInterceptor, AuditInterceptor. Chain executes before/after each command.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Both Camunda and Flowable use this pattern successfully. Low implementation cost, high value. Essential for UML model editors with undo/redo.

components.name: Bidirectional XML/XMI Serialization
components.value_proposition: Lossless round-trip: XML → Model → XML preserving extensions, comments, formatting. Namespace-aware parsing. Essential for UML tool interoperability via XMI standard.
risks: XMI more complex than BPMN XML
components.notes: XMI 2.5.1 support required. Handle: UML namespace, XMI namespace, profile namespaces, vendor extensions. Preserve unknown elements for tool interoperability.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Critical for UML. Both engines handle BPMN XML well with extension preservation. UML XMI more complex but same patterns apply.

components.name: Qualification Function Pattern
components.value_proposition: Structural classification: classify objects by examining structure, not explicit types. Duck typing in strongly-typed system. Applicable to UML: infer stereotypes, detect patterns, validate conformance.
risks: Can become brittle with model changes
components.notes: Use for: detecting design patterns in UML models, suggesting stereotypes, validating architectural conformance. Example: isRepository(class) checks if class has CRUD methods.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Clever pattern from FINOS. Not core priority but useful for advanced features like pattern detection and code smell detection.

components.name: Multi-Layer Validation Framework
components.value_proposition: 4-layer validation: Syntax (grammar) → Type checking → Constraints (cardinality, choice) → Semantic (cross-model). Clear error messages with element paths. Essential for UML model validation.
components.notes: Python validators: 1) XMI schema validation, 2) Metaclass type checking, 3) OCL constraint evaluation, 4) Well-formedness rules. Return structured ValidationResult with paths.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Standard pattern across all analyzed projects. Well-understood, proven approach. Must-have for UML tooling.

components.name: Service-Oriented API Design
components.value_proposition: 8-12 focused services with single responsibilities. Better than monolithic API. Examples: ModelService (CRUD), DiagramService (layout), ValidationService, TransformationService, GenerationService.
components.notes: For UML-Codex: ModelService, DiagramService, ValidationService, TransformationService, CodeGenerationService, ProfileService, OCLService, ExportService. Each service has clear responsibility.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Both workflow engines use this successfully. Scales well, testable, clear boundaries. Standard best practice.

components.name: Spring Boot Auto-Configuration
components.value_proposition: Convention over configuration. Auto-detect components, configure datasources, setup defaults. Flowable provides flowable-spring-boot-starter. Great developer experience.
components.notes: Consider Python equivalent with FastAPI or Django. Create uml-codex-fastapi with auto-discovery of: models, validators, generators, services. Configuration via environment or config files.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Spring Boot integration is key to Flowable's adoption. Python equivalent would be FastAPI with dependency injection and auto-discovery.

components.name: Schema-Driven UI Generation
components.value_proposition: Rosetta DSL → TypeScript models → Angular components → Dynamic tree UI. Type-specific editors (Boolean, Date, Enum, etc.). Real-time validation. Applicable to UML for property editors and diagram tools.
components.notes: Pattern: UML Metamodel → Python/TypeScript models → React components → Property editors + Diagram canvas. Use modern stack: React 18+, TypeScript 5+, Vite, TanStack.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Good pattern but implementation outdated. Adapt concept to modern React/TypeScript stack. Lower priority - backend more critical initially.

components.name: Resource-Based Test Data Pattern
components.value_proposition: Complex test objects as JSON/XMI files in resources/. Load in tests: model = load_test_model('class-diagram-01.xmi'). Version controlled, shareable, realistic data.
components.notes: Simple pattern, high value. tests/resources/models/ with .xmi files. tests/resources/diagrams/ with diagram data. Helper: load_model(filename), load_diagram(filename).
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Simple, proven pattern. Low implementation cost. Enables comprehensive testing with realistic UML models.

components.name: Completeness Checking Pattern
components.value_proposition: Enumerate all possible model element types. Ensure handler for each. Fail loudly if missing. Prevents silent feature omissions. Critical for code generation correctness.
components.notes: Python: Use Enum for all UML metaclasses. In handlers, use match/case (3.10+) or if/elif with final else: raise NotImplementedError(). Consider mypy exhaustiveness checking.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Critical lesson from REGnosys issues. Python generator missing features caused bugs. Must fail loudly, not silently ignore.

components.name: Execution Tree Model
components.value_proposition: Parent-child execution tree for concurrent execution and scope isolation. Natural model for Activity Diagram fork/join and State Machine orthogonal regions. More intuitive than Camunda's approach.
components.notes: For UML: Root execution for Activity Diagram. Child executions for each forked path. Join synchronizes children. State Machines: parent for composite state, children for orthogonal regions.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Flowable's tree model cleaner than Camunda. Parent-child relationships natural for UML concurrency semantics.

components.name: History Event Stream
components.value_proposition: Audit trail of all changes. Events: ElementCreated, AttributeChanged, AssociationAdded, etc. Enables undo/redo, change tracking, collaboration features. Useful for UML model versioning.
components.notes: Start simple: event log to database. Later: event sourcing with replay. Events: ModelElementEvent with type, element ID, timestamp, user, change details.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Both engines support history. Not critical for v1.0 but important for collaboration and versioning. Design event structure early even if storage deferred.

components.name: Manager-Based Persistence Pattern
components.value_proposition: Specialized manager per entity type (ModelElementManager, DiagramManager, etc.). Encapsulates database operations. Both engines use MyBatis.
components.notes: Study pattern but use SQLAlchemy (Python) or JPA (Java) instead of MyBatis. Manager pattern still useful: isolates persistence logic, enables mocking, clear responsibilities.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Pattern good, technology choice (MyBatis) less ideal. Modern ORMs (SQLAlchemy, JPA) provide better abstraction and maintenance.

components.name: Expression Language Integration
components.value_proposition: Runtime expression evaluation for guards, constraints, assignments. JUEL (Java), Groovy, JavaScript support. For UML: OCL constraint evaluation essential.
components.notes: Options: 1) Custom OCL implementation, 2) Eclipse OCL (Java), 3) PyOCL (Python), 4) Subset of OCL with Python eval. Start with simple constraint language, expand to full OCL.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: OCL critical for UML but complex. Both engines use existing expression libraries. Recommend: start with simple subset, use Eclipse OCL or build custom gradually.

components.name: Diagram Auto-Layout Algorithms
components.value_proposition: Automatic layout of BPMN diagrams. Useful for UML: auto-arrange class diagrams, sequence diagrams. Improves UX for generated diagrams.
components.notes: Consider existing libraries: GraphViz (dot), dagre, ELK (Eclipse Layout Kernel). For UML: hierarchical layout for class diagrams, sequence for sequence diagrams, orthogonal for state machines.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Nice-to-have feature. Many existing libraries. Lower priority - manual layout sufficient for v1.0.

components.name: Multi-Database Dialect Support
components.value_proposition: Support 6+ databases with dialect-specific optimizations. Both engines hand-write SQL per database. Performance varies 10x across databases.
components.notes: AVOID hand-written SQL per database. Use ORM (SQLAlchemy, JPA) for abstraction. Test on 2-3 databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite). Provide migration scripts.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Both engines struggle with this. Hand-written SQL is maintenance burden. Modern ORMs solve this. Start with single database, add others via ORM if needed.

components.name: Process Migration Framework
components.value_proposition: Migrate running process instances to new process definition versions. Complex but enables model evolution without disrupting running instances.
components.notes: Not applicable to UML modeling tool initially. Relevant if UML-Codex includes execution engine for Activity Diagrams / State Machines. Defer to v2.0+.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Interesting feature but not core UML need. Only relevant if building execution engine. Low priority.

components.name: Pluggable Storage Abstraction
components.value_proposition: Innovation from Flowable issues: in-memory DataManagers using ConcurrentMap for extreme throughput (100s of processes/second). Pluggable storage enables SQL (persistent) or in-memory (performance).
components.notes: For UML-Codex: ModelRepository interface with implementations: InMemoryModelRepository (ConcurrentMap), SQLModelRepository (SQLAlchemy). Enables fast prototyping (in-memory) and production (SQL).
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Excellent idea from Flowable community. Enables flexibility: dev/test use in-memory, production uses SQL. Clean abstraction.

components.name: Namespace Registry and Resolution
components.value_proposition: Central registry for XML namespaces. Maps namespace URIs to prefixes and element types. Essential for UML XMI parsing with multiple namespaces (UML, XMI, profiles, vendor extensions).
components.notes: Python: NamespaceRegistry with register_namespace(uri, prefix, schema). Parser uses registry to resolve element types. Support for: UML namespace, XMI namespace, profile namespaces, vendor extensions.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Critical for XMI parsing. Camunda handles BPMN namespaces well. UML has more namespaces (profiles) but same pattern applies.

components.name: Optimistic Locking with Version Fields
components.value_proposition: Version field on entities. Increment on each update. Detect concurrent modifications. Enables collaborative editing without pessimistic locks.
components.notes: Standard pattern with ORMs. SQLAlchemy supports version_id_col. Detect conflicts, notify user, provide merge UI. Start simple: last-write-wins with conflict detection.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Standard pattern for collaborative editing. Both engines use successfully. Low implementation cost with ORM support.

components.name: AssertJ Fluent Test Assertions
components.value_proposition: Fluent assertions: assertThat(model).hasElements(3).hasClass('Person').hasAttribute('name'). Better readability than plain asserts. Python equivalent: assertpy.
components.notes: Python: use assertpy. from assertpy import assert_that. assert_that(model.classes).extracting('name').contains('Person', 'Company'). Improves test readability significantly.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Flowable tests very readable with AssertJ. Python assertpy provides similar fluent API. Low cost, high value for test quality.

components.name: Good First Issue Labeling
components.value_proposition: Label simple issues 'good first issue' to encourage community contributions. Reduces maintainer burden, builds community.
components.notes: Community building practice. Not technical but valuable for open source projects. Label issues: good-first-issue, help-wanted, documentation, testing.
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Community practice from Flowable. If UML-Codex goes open source, useful for community building. Low priority until project public.

components.name: Configuration Validation on Startup
components.value_proposition: Validate configuration at startup. Fail fast with clear error messages. Issue #4066: retry configuration properties silently ignored, causing confusion. Prevent misconfiguration bugs.
components.notes: Python: use Pydantic Settings for configuration validation. Define schema with constraints. Validate on app startup. Clear error messages: 'Invalid OCL timeout: -1. Must be positive integer.'
evaluation_notes: 2025-11-08: Important lesson from Flowable issues. Silent config failures waste developer time. Validate early, fail fast, clear messages.
